methods.note: Page 8 text supports the high-level method: PACT is a SPICE-based compact RC simulator on Xyce 6.12 with OpenMPI 3.1.4, run at MGHPCC with up to 112 cores. It also supports the HotSpot comparison on a 256-core SCC-inspired 2-D chip scaled to 22 nm, using the same medium-cost heat sink. The paper's SCC result is a simulation-time speedup, not a temperature. The extraction's experiment kind 'custom_2d_steady' therefore does not match the paper's observable. The 3-D and transient solver features (Table IV mixes the monolithic 3-D and SCC rows) are not a 2-D reproduction.

code.note: The only code links are the PACT and OpenSTA GitHub URLs (pages 2 and 7). No asset text, pinned commit or file excerpt is in the packet, so a bare URL is not evidence. Nothing shows that SCC inputs, configs or power files exist.

parameters.note: Table III (grid resolution, die size, layer stack, materials, heat spreader and heat sink parameters) and Table IV (core counts, times, speedups) are image tables on page 8 and were not visually verified. Only the 216.6 W/cm2 hot-spot density, the 1.9x/232x maxima and the 112-core limit are supported by text. The unit conversion to 2,166,000 W/m2 is arithmetically correct but is a density only.

config.note: The exact solver choice, grid size, heat sink settings and core count for the SCC steady-state run are in Table III or IV and were not seen. The text only says PACT 'automatically uses AztecOO' at finer grids. KLU, AztecOO and TRAP are described generally, so none can be pinned to this scenario. No Studio package or material assumptions are supplied.

data.note: The floorplan is empty: there are no block names, x/y/width/height values, or per-block watts. Total chip power is not stated and the power profile (Eris et al., ref [20]) is not supplied. Same-scenario power for every block is therefore absent. No temperature observable (value, unit, location, aggregation) exists for the SCC scenario. The roughly 90 degC on page 11 belongs to the OpenROAD MPSoC experiment.

findings.reason: A 2-D steady experiment cannot be built or approved. No block geometry or per-block power is available, and the paper's SCC result is a timing and speedup comparison, not a steady temperature.
